text: prove that sin(x)/x approaches 1 as x approaches 0, and explain it

Given: Angles are measured in radians., The unit circle has radius \(1\)., Initially, \(0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}\)., The unit-circle regions satisfy triangle \(OAB\subseteq\text{sector }OBA\subseteq\triangle OBT\)., The function \(\sin x/x\) is considered for \(x\neq0\).
Find: \(\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin x}{x}\)

1. State the domain and the target limit
   lim ₓ→ ₀(sin x)/(x)=1
   We measure angles in radians. We first prove the result for \(0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}\), where the unit-circle geometry is easiest to describe. The expression is defined for \(x\neq 0\).

2. Construct the labelled unit-circle diagram
   O=(0,0), A=(cos x,sin x), B=(1,0)
   Draw the unit circle with centre \(O\). Let \(B=(1,0)\), and let the radius making angle \(x\) with the positive horizontal axis end at \(A=(\cos x,\sin x)\). The sector \(OBA\) lies between the two radii, while the tangent at \(B\) meets the ray \(OA\) at a point \(T\). The diagram should label the angle \(x\), the triangle \(OAB\), the sector \(OBA\), and the outer triangle \(OBT\).

3. Compute the area of the inner triangle
   [triangle OAB]=frac 12lvert OArvert lvert OBrvert sin x=frac 12sin x
   Both radii have length \(1\), and the included angle is \(x\). Therefore the area of triangle \(OAB\) is \(\frac12\cdot 1\cdot 1\cdot\sin x=\frac12\sin x\).

4. Compute the area of the sector
   [sector OBA]=frac 12 x
   For a unit circle, the area of a sector with radian angle \(x\) is \(\frac12 r^2x\). Since \(r=1\), its area is \(\frac12x\). This is precisely where the radian assumption is used.

5. Compute the area of the outer tangent triangle
   [triangle OBT]=frac 12tan x
   The tangent at \(B\) is the vertical line \(x=1\). Since the ray \(OA\) makes angle \(x\) with the horizontal axis, its intersection with this tangent has height \(BT=\tan x\). Thus \(OB=1\) and \([\triangle OBT]=\frac12\cdot 1\cdot\tan x=\frac12\tan x\).

6. Use containment of the three regions
   frac 12sin xle frac 12xle frac 12tan x
   For \(0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}\), triangle \(OAB\) lies inside the sector, and the sector lies inside triangle \(OBT\). Areas therefore satisfy \([\triangle OAB]\le[\text{sector }OBA]\le[\triangle OBT]\). Substituting the three area formulas gives the displayed inequality.

7. Remove the common positive factor
   sin xle xle tan x
   Multiply every part of the inequality by \(2>0\). The order is preserved, giving \(\sin x\le x\le\tan x\).

8. Convert the geometric inequality into the squeeze bounds
   sin xle xle (sin x)/(cos x)
   Replace \(\tan x\) by \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\). Because \(0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}\), both \(x\) and \(\cos x\) are positive.

9. Derive the upper bound
   sin xle x Longrightarrow (sin x)/(x)le 1
   Since \(x>0\), divide the left inequality \(\sin x\le x\) by \(x\). This gives the upper bound \(\frac{\sin x}{x}\le 1\).

10. Derive the lower bound
   xle (sin x)/(cos x) Longrightarrow xcos xle sin x Longrightarrow cos xle (sin x)/(x)
   Starting from \(x\le\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\), multiply by the positive number \(\cos x\), obtaining \(x\cos x\le\sin x\). Then divide by the positive number \(x\), obtaining \(\cos x\le\frac{\sin x}{x}\).

11. Complete the positive-side squeeze inequality
   cos xle (sin x)/(x)le 1 (0<x<(π)/(2) )
   Combining the lower bound from the tangent triangle with the upper bound from the inner triangle gives the desired two-sided inequality for positive \(x\) near zero.

12. Extend the bounds to negative x by evenness
   (sin (-x))/(-x)=(sin x)/(x)
   Using the oddness identity \(\sin(-x)=-\sin x\), we obtain \(\frac{\sin(-x)}{-x}=\frac{\sin x}{x}\). Thus \(\frac{\sin x}{x}\) is even. The positive-side inequality therefore applies symmetrically for negative \(x\) with \(0<|x|<\frac{\pi}{2}\).

13. Take the limits of the bounding functions
   lim ₓ→₀cos x=cos 0=1, lim ₓ→₀1=1
   Cosine is continuous at zero, so its limit as \(x\to0\) is \(\cos0=1\). The constant function \(1\) also has limit \(1\). Therefore the lower and upper bounds approach the same number.

14. Apply the squeeze theorem
   cos xle (sin x)/(x)le 1 and lim ₓ→₀cos x=lim ₓ→₀1=1 Longrightarrow lim ₓ→₀(sin x)/(x)=1
   The squeeze theorem states that if a function lies between two functions having the same limit, then it has that same limit. Since \(\frac{\sin x}{x}\) is squeezed between \(\cos x\) and \(1\), its limit is \(1\). This establishes the result from both sides of zero.

Answer: boxed lim ₓ→₀(sin x)/(x)=1
For \(0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}\), the unit-circle area comparison gives \(\frac12\sin x\le\frac12x\le\frac12\tan x\), hence \(\cos x\le\frac{\sin x}{x}\le1\). Since \(\frac{\sin x}{x}\) is even, the same bounds hold for negative \(x\) near zero. Both bounds tend to \(1\) as \(x\to0\), so the squeeze theorem yields \(\boxed{\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin x}{x}=1}\).

operations.title: The target limit
operations.caption: \lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\sin x}{x}=1
operations.narration: We measure angles in radians and begin with positive angles between zero and pi over two. Our goal is to understand what sin x divided by x approaches as x approaches zero.

operations.title: The unit-circle picture
operations.caption: O=(0,0),\qquad A=(\cos x,\sin x),\qquad B=(1,0)
operations.narration: Draw a unit circle with center O. Let B be the point one unit to the right, and let the radius at angle x end at A. The ray OA meets the tangent at B at T.

operations.title: Inner triangle area
operations.caption: [\triangle OAB]=\frac12\lvert OA\rvert\lvert OB\rvert\sin x=\frac12\sin x
operations.narration: Both radii have length one. The area formula for two sides and their included angle gives the area of triangle OAB as one half sin x.

operations.title: Sector area
operations.caption: [\text{sector }OBA]=\frac12x
operations.narration: A sector with radius one and radian angle x has area one half times x. This simple formula is exactly where radians enter the proof.

operations.title: Outer triangle area
operations.caption: [\triangle OBT]=\frac12\tan x
operations.narration: The tangent at B is vertical. Since OA makes angle x with the horizontal, its height at the tangent is tan x. So the outer triangle has area one half tan x.

operations.title: Containment gives bounds
operations.caption: \frac12\sin x\le \frac12x\le \frac12\tan x
operations.narration: For a positive angle less than pi over two, the inner triangle lies inside the sector, and the sector lies inside the tangent triangle. Their areas therefore increase from left to right.

operations.title: Remove the common factor
operations.caption: \sin x\le x\le\tan x
operations.narration: Multiply every part by two. Because two is positive, the order does not change.

operations.title: Rewrite tangent
operations.caption: \sin x\le x\le\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}
operations.narration: Use tan x equals sin x over cos x. In our domain, x and cos x are both positive, so the next divisions will be safe.

operations.title: The upper bound
operations.caption: \sin x\le x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \frac{\sin x}{x}\le 1
operations.narration: From sin x less than or equal to x, divide by the positive number x. This places sin x over x below one.

operations.title: The lower bound
operations.caption: x\le\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x\cos x\le\sin x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \cos x\le\frac{\sin x}{x}
operations.narration: Start with x less than or equal to sin x over cos x. Multiply by positive cos x, then divide by positive x. The result places cos x below sin x over x.

operations.title: Positive-side squeeze
operations.caption: \cos x\le\frac{\sin x}{x}\le 1\qquad\left(0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}\right)
operations.narration: Combining the two results gives the complete squeeze for positive x near zero.

operations.title: Symmetry across zero
operations.caption: \frac{\sin(-x)}{-x}=\frac{\sin x}{x}
operations.narration: Because sine is odd, changing x to negative x changes both the numerator and denominator's signs. The signs cancel, so the ratio is even and the same bounds apply on the negative side.

operations.title: Both bounds converge
operations.caption: \lim_{x\to0}\cos x=\cos 0=1,\qquad \lim_{x\to0}1=1
operations.narration: As x approaches zero, cosine approaches cos zero, which is one. The constant upper bound is already one. Both sides therefore meet at the same limiting value.

operations.title: Apply the squeeze theorem
operations.caption: \cos x\le\frac{\sin x}{x}\le 1\quad\text{and}\quad \lim_{x\to0}\cos x=\lim_{x\to0}1=1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin x}{x}=1
operations.narration: A function trapped between two functions with the same limit must share that limit. Therefore sin x over x approaches one from both sides of zero.

operations.title: FINAL ANSWER
operations.caption: \boxed{\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin x}{x}=1}
operations.narration: Thus, when x is measured in radians, the ratio of sin x to x approaches one as x approaches zero from either side. Near zero, sin x is approximately x.
